jane.cust: Hi — customer hitting a 400 when using function-calling to invoke files.read. Error from API: \"ToolCallValidationError: Malformed tool args: Invalid JSON at offset 47 (Unexpected token '\\' or single quote)\". Posting the request body we send below.

jane.cust: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{
    "model":"redwood-2",
    "function_call": {"name":"files.read"},
    "function_args": "{\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\jane\\projects\\${userId}\\notes.txt\", \"include_metadata\": true,}\""
  }'
```

jane.cust: Observed behavior: API returns 400 and we can't reach the tool. We tried stripping headers, same result.

alex.support: Thanks — this looks like two problems in the payload: (1) you're sending function_args as a raw string that contains unescaped backslashes and a trailing comma, and (2) the template `${userId}` is not expanded client-side and ends up inside the JSON string. Both will break the JSON parser.

alex.support: Quick repro steps for us: try sending function_args as an object (not a serialized string), or if you must send a string, run `JSON.stringify` on a JS object instead of building the JSON manually. Example below.

alex.support: Correct (JS SDK) — pass args as object:```
await client.call({
  model: 'redwood-2',
  function_call: { name: 'files.read' },
  function_args: {
    path: 'C:\\Users\\jane\\projects\\12345\\notes.txt',
    include_metadata: true
  }
});
```

alex.support: If you must embed JSON into a string field (not recommended), escape backslashes and remove trailing commas:```
"{\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\jane\\projects\\12345\\notes.txt\",\"include_metadata\":true}"
```

mike.dev: can repro locally with the curl payload. The parser fails on the first `\\` sequence because the outer single-quoted curl JSON contains unescaped backslashes inside a quoted string. Also the trailing comma after `true,` triggers a strict JSON error.

mike.dev: short workaround for now: ensure your templating expands `${userId}` before serializing. In our customer case the template engine returns the literal `${userId}` because it wasn't executed in the client context.

jane.cust: ah — we were building the JSON with a template literal but then wrapped it in single quotes for the curl - so expansion didn't happen in the service that builds the payload. We'll try the object approach.

alex.support: Also, if you keep hitting this, please paste the exact `function_args` value you send (as raw text) and the SDK / curl client version. We can add a more helpful validation message to reject unescaped paths earlier.

eng-oncall-bot: Deploy note: schema-validator v2 rolled out earlier today (12:17 UTC) — monitoring parse-error rates for function_args.

eli.sre: tagging eng-runtime for visibility; if we see repeat incidents we should add a client-side lint that detects unescaped windows paths + trailing commas.

mike.dev: filing a quick internal repro: `npm run repro --case=unescaped-windows-path` and will attach unit test.

jane.cust: thanks all. I'll try the object payload. If still failing I'll paste what I send. :thumbsup:
